clusters.name: Teodor's death, 1978–1979
clusters.reason: Around your grandfather Teodor's death in January 1978, within the following year: your grandmother Delphine stopped cooking and went to her mother Odette's every evening; your father Duncan took night shifts and distanced from Odette; your uncle Anton drank at lunch with a warning at work; Odette lay awake over them; and your brother Callum had ear infections all winter. Delphine took a job at the library by May 1979. The shifts across these months show the family's reaction as it moved from person to person.

clusters.name: Odette's pregnancy, 1984
clusters.reason: Around your mother Odette ordered to bed for the rest of her pregnancy in March 1984: your grandmother Hazel came every morning to keep the house, then argued with your father Duncan over how she kept it; your brother Callum stammered again after a year free of it. These shifts within four months belong together around the upheaval in the household, and no one else's shifts show in those months.

clusters.name: Hazel's Parkinson's diagnosis, 1986–1996
clusters.reason: Around your grandmother Hazel diagnosed with Parkinson's in September 1986, over the following decade: your grandfather Ambrose took over her cooking and appointments; your father Duncan phoned his father every night for news of her, then argued with his uncle Lyle over who should help; Ambrose developed chest pains; and Duncan drank most evenings and fought with Odette over his time at his parents' house. The shifts climb over years with only partial relief between them—Hazel's fall in 1988, a new medicine steadying her in 1988, then her decline again—until she moved to the nursing home in June 1997 and Duncan cut his drinking back to weekends by October.

clusters.name: Callum leaving home, 1999–2000
clusters.reason: Around your brother Callum leaving home for a job up north in May 1999: your father Duncan and Callum argued most nights over his plans; your mother Odette could not settle at the thought of him so far away; Duncan missed days at work and sat up late in the garage; your sister Ines skipped school most of that autumn; and Odette took Ines with her everywhere. By August 2000 Ines was back at school full days and passed her exams. The shifts pass from one person to the next as the household held Callum's absence.

By November you took a job at the garden centre and slept through the night again. Every shift in these months is yours, and no one else's shows then.
